open-question.question: Does the draft adopt the 2026-11-19 conversation's new-mission button, which takes a typed goal and opens an interactive `discuss-mission-goal` session on it in a terminal, where the person carries the conversation on: as stated, in a refined form, or not at all? The draft's one way to start a mission today is the headless chain of the usage page, its `<goal>` and `<scope>` typed into an input box.

Does the draft adopt the 2026-11-19 conversation's one pane with a page per mission, on which a mission's questions, tasks, and buttons stand together, and if so does it replace the draft's side-bar tree of missions and its custom editor claiming `open_questions.xml`, or stand beside either? The draft's VS Code check names no pane other than the custom editor.

Which states of a mission does the extension tell apart, from what does it read them, and does a state only show or also decide which buttons are offered: the `started` or `defined` of `missions.py live` with the open-question and task lists, or the finer states `ideas/kepala.md` names (Scoped through Done), which that draft reads from the last run's fixed first line?

A task section holds a title and a brief with no field for a kind of work, the maintainer's largest mission held about 140 tasks, and the draft's constraint has the extension write nothing under a mission directory.

When a task runs under a host, model, and effort chosen for it, is its command line one of the recipe file's own single-task lines picked by name, so the extension still holds no host flag, model name, or effort level of its own, or does the extension compose the line from the three values and so hold each host's command syntax?

Where the extension orders runs itself (a task loop, a bounded repeat), how does the draft place that logic against the orchestrator `ideas/kepala.md` outlines: as the interface-independent part Kepala may reuse, as a first form of Kepala itself, or left out, with all automatic ordering kept for Kepala? Where do the interactive command lines behind the extension's buttons come from, the `discuss-open-question` session the question view opens and any `discuss-mission-goal` session a new-mission button opens, given that `docs/ways-of-using.md` holds only headless lines and the draft has the extension hold no host flag or model name of its own?

Does the question view show each question collapsed to its title and its pick until the person opens it, to fit the maintainer's report that most questions are screened by their heading alone and only one or two are read in full, or does it show every question whole as the draft describes?

Does the revised draft record the reasons the 2026-11-19 conversation gives for the extension (a host offers two usable layers, an agent and its subagents, so what orders the skills sits outside it; VS Code supplies the terminal and git integration an application of its own would have to build; the extension is an experiment that a deeper integration or such an application may follow), and if so where in the draft?

Where does the VS Code extension's code live: in a repository of its own, as `ideas/kepala.md` plans for the orchestrator, or in a directory of this repository outside `core/` that is rendered into no host tree?
open-question.alternative: The extension's code lives in a repository of its own, beside this one and apart from the one `ideas/kepala.md` plans for the orchestrator. It carries its own TypeScript and Node toolchain, CI, and release. Whatever it takes from the plugin's contract (the recipe lines, the fixed console lines) is a copy pinned to a stated plugin version or read at run time. This repository gains no file, toolchain, or CI step. This repository stays stdlib-only Python, Markdown, and one build script under its one-job CI, and the extension releases on its own schedule, as `ideas/benchmark.md` plans for the benchmark: a separate project that takes Gurita as an input and records the commit it exercised. Every copy of the contract is explicit and its plugin version is named. The copies of the recipe page and the fixed-line table can fall behind the plugin, since no test in this repository sees them. A plugin change that moves a line breaks the extension unnoticed until it is next run against the new release, and a change touching both means two commits in two repositories. How much there is to copy depends on how the sibling questions settle the recipe source and the live-state source.

The extension's code lives in the repository `ideas/kepala.md` plans for the orchestrator, so the extension and Kepala are two parts of one project outside this repository, with one toolchain, CI, and release between them. This repository gains nothing, as under the own-repository option. Whatever ordering logic the extension and Kepala share sits in one checkout and one test suite rather than being copied between two outside repositories, and both copy the plugin's contract once, against one pinned plugin version. It ties the extension, which the 2026-11-19 conversation calls an experiment in the maintainer's own environment, to an orchestrator that is only an outline with nothing decided, and it brings a repository that does not exist yet into being for the extension's sake. It works only if the Kepala-boundary question places the extension's ordering logic as part of Kepala or as a part Kepala reuses. The contract copies drift as under the own-repository option.

The extension's code lives in a directory of this repository outside `core/`, rendered into no host tree, and its build and tests, including a check of its recipes and fixed lines against `docs/ways-of-using.md` and the `## Fixed console lines` table, run as steps of the existing one-job drift-gate workflow. It is released from this repository beside the three host trees. The extension reads the recipe page and the fixed-line table where they stand, one checkout away, so a plugin change and the extension change it needs land in one commit and the CI fails on drift as it already does for `hosts/`. No copy of the contract exists to fall behind. It puts a second toolchain (Node, TypeScript, packaging, a Marketplace publisher) into the one CI job every plugin change runs, slowing and widening the gate for all plugin work and making `/release-plugin` handle a fourth artifact. A Node failure then blocks a change to the Python tools.

The extension's code lives in a directory of this repository outside `core/`, rendered into no host tree, but its toolchain stays out of the existing drift-gate job: it is built, tested, and published by hand from that directory or by a workflow of its own, and its release is not part of `/release-plugin`. The contract stays one checkout away and a change touching both the plugin and the extension can land in one commit, while every plugin change keeps the stdlib-only one-job gate it has today and the release skill stays unchanged. Nothing in the plugin's gate fails when the extension falls behind the page or the table, so the in-repository home loses most of its advantage over a separate repository while still adding a Node project, its lock file, and its ignored build output to a repository that holds none today. CLAUDE.md's layout and the contributor guide gain an entry for it.

The extension starts in a directory of this repository outside `core/`, rendered into no host tree and kept out of the drift-gate job, while it is the maintainer's experiment, and the draft states the condition under which it moves to a repository of its own: before it is first published, or once it outlives the experiment. It fits the conversation's framing of the extension as an experiment that a deeper integration or an application of its own may follow: the first form costs no new repository and stays next to the contract while the recipe and fixed-line reads are still being worked out, and the separate home is taken only once the extension proves worth keeping. It plans a move, with its history split or carried over by hand and every path the draft and the contract copies name rewritten then, and it leaves the trigger for that move as one more judgment the draft has to state and someone has to make. Until the move the repository carries the Node project, as under the outside-CI option.

open-question.question: What are the extension's shipped recipes read from: the chains of `docs/ways-of-using.md` parsed as the page stands, a data file the page is written from or checked against, or the blocks of `snippets/GURITA_USAGE.md`, tracked since 2026-11-18, whose first-run, requirements-iteration, and execution blocks are the ones the 2026-11-19 conversation turns into one button each?

Is a recipe only a flat list of command lines, clicked again for each further requirements iteration, or may it carry a bounded repeat that ends when the review prints its convergence line? The maintainer reports going from the first run straight to execution for the easiest work, one requirements iteration for harder work, and a third about once a month.

Where does the extension run a headless command line: typed into the person's terminal and followed through shell integration, as a child process of the extension outside any terminal, or under a runner started as a terminal's own process that starts each line of a chain itself?

From what does the extension read how a headless run ended: the first line of the run's plain final message, matched against the fixed console lines, or the structured output each host offers (`--output-format stream-json` on Claude Code and Antigravity, `--json` on Codex), which adds a flag the pasted line does not carry?

If a runner process carries out a chain's lines, what is it written in and where does it ship: stdlib-only Python, which needs only the `python3` the plugin already requires, or the extension's own language, and inside the extension or as a plugin tool found at the plugin's installed location? A plugin tool can only be stdlib-only Python.

Does a chain run as one shell session, so that a shell step of the person's own in a recipe (sourcing an environment file, a shell function) takes effect for the lines after it, and with that how does a substituted value such as a Short Title or a typed answer reach a line: as an argument no shell parses, escaped for the line's quoting, or refused when it holds a character special there?

From what does the extension read which missions are live and whether each is started: the plugin's installed `missions.py`, which needs the plugin's installed location found per host, or a glob of the discovery pattern in the workspace, which needs no install but is a second copy of the pattern and cannot tell `started` from `defined`?
What turns `open_questions.xml` into the extension's question view: a reader of the XML inside the extension, or a read-only render added to the plugin's tools, whose output the view shows?

For which hosts does the extension ship command lines: the chains as `docs/ways-of-using.md` writes them (Claude Code lines, one mixed-host chain, and a legend for moving a line to another host), or each chain also written out per host?

Where is the extension published: the Visual Studio Marketplace only, or also a registry the VS Code forks read? The 2026-11-19 conversation calls the extension an experiment in the maintainer's own environment, and the draft's check did not cover publication outside the Marketplace.

What is the extension named: a name that joins Gurita and Kepala, or a descriptive one? Whichever it is, its slug is to get the direct registry lookup `ideas/gurita.md` records its own first check lacked.

What does the revision do with the facts in the draft that have moved since it was written on 2026-11-17 (the fixed-line count, now 87 rather than 94; the live-mission and answer-commit counts; the snippet file, now tracked as `snippets/GURITA_USAGE.md` with two placeholders rather than personal and untracked): bring them all to today's values under a new date, correct only those a decision of this mission touches, or leave the dated sections as written?

Does this mission check the VS Code documentation for what its decisions newly rely on (a pane other than the custom editor, the side-bar tree, publication outside the Marketplace) and record the result in the draft's dated check section, or does it list each as an unchecked unknown among the draft's questions for the work?

How does the revised draft record each choice this mission settles, the ten former questions and the adopted ideas alike: as a dated entry with its reason under the draft's Decided section beside the section text it changes, only as that section text with the question removed, or only as a Decided entry?
